\subsection{Purpose}




This section converts the prior strategy files into a 90-day execution system.




It is not a market research document. It is an operating plan for moving from thesis completion and portfolio preparation into structured international applications, interviews, negotiation, and offer evaluation.

\subsection{Operating principle}




The plan prioritizes \textbf{visible proof of skill} over additional passive learning.




The critical path is:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
TwinSight proof → portfolio MVP → LinkedIn/CV/GitHub alignment → targeted applications → interviews → offer evaluation
\end{mdcode}




The plan should not be interrupted by:




\begin{itemize}
\item starting a new major project;
\item rewriting the thesis unnecessarily;
\item taking long courses without output;
\item polishing low-relevance repositories;
\item targeting unrelated full-stack jobs too early;
\item waiting for Portuguese citizenship before applying;
\item treating Germany as the immediate employment base.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{90-day outcome targets}




By the end of 90 days, the expected state should be:




\begin{enumerate}
\item A public-facing portfolio MVP exists.
\item TwinSight X500 has a recruiter-ready case study.
\item GitHub no longer looks unfocused.
\item LinkedIn and CV match the same positioning.
\item At least 120 companies have been classified.
\item At least 80–150 targeted applications or outreach actions have been made.
\item At least 8–15 recruiter or hiring-manager conversations have been attempted.
\item At least 3–6 interview processes have been initiated.
\item Offer evaluation criteria are operational.
\item A 12-month skill roadmap is active.
\end{enumerate}




These targets are not guarantees. They are execution metrics.

\subsubsection{Actions}




\begin{itemize}
\item Stop applying to weak C targets unless cashflow requires it.
\item Increase outreach to A1/A2.

\item Reuse TwinSight in technical messages.
\item Ask for referrals where possible.

\subsubsection{Offer evaluation model}

\begin{center}

\midrule
\endhead

Net compensation & 15 \\
Role fit & 20 \\
Portfolio leverage & 15 \\

Remote stability & 10 \\
Learning ROI & 5 \\
EU leverage & 5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




Reject or renegotiate if:




\begin{itemize}
\item total score is low;
\item payment terms are vague;
\item unpaid trial is large;
\item exclusivity is broad;
\item IP terms are abusive;
\item salary is below minimum;
\item role dilutes the portfolio.
\end{itemize}

\item portfolio link;
\item tracker entry.
\end{itemize}




\subsubsection{C-priority}




Requires:




\begin{itemize}
\item fast application;
\item no heavy customization;
\item no deep portfolio rewrite.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Stop conditions}




Stop following up if:




\begin{itemize}
\item company rejects;
\item no response after three messages;
\item role is filled;
\item role requires unavailable work authorization;
\item compensation is below minimum;
\item company shows red flags.
\end{itemize}

\section{11. Decision gates}




\subsection{Gate 1 — Day 30}




Proceed to scaled applications only if:




\begin{itemize}
\item CV ready;
\item LinkedIn updated;
\item TwinSight visible;
\item GitHub acceptable;
\item portfolio MVP live or shareable;
\item tracker active.
\end{itemize}




If not, extend Phase 1 by one week.




\subsection{Gate 2 — Day 60}




Continue current strategy only if:




\begin{itemize}
\item replies exist;
\item interviews exist or seem close;
\item portfolio feedback is not negative;
\item target roles still fit.
\end{itemize}




If not, adjust:




\begin{center}
\scriptsize
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.455\linewidth}}
\toprule

\toprule
Failure & Adjustment \\
\midrule
\endhead
No replies & Rewrite positioning \\
Wrong replies & Change target list \\
Low offers & Raise company tier \\
Technical failures & Skill sprint \\
Portfolio confusion & Simplify projects \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\end{center}




\subsection{Gate 3 — Day 90}




Decide:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Continue / Pivot / Add fallback / Skill sprint / Accept offer
\end{mdcode}




The decision must be based on tracker evidence, not mood.

\section{13. What not to do during the 90 days}




Do not:




\begin{itemize}
\item rebuild the portfolio from scratch more than once;
\item start a new flagship project;
\item present ARA as the thesis;
\item claim EU work authorization before it exists;
\item apply broadly as full-stack unless necessary;
\item spend more time on courses than portfolio;
\item publish incomplete weak repos;
\item overexplain AI usage defensively;
\item accept vague unpaid trials;
\item accept broad non-competes;
\item ignore gross-to-net calculations;
\item wait passively for recruiters.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{14. Final 90-day operating statement}




The operational target for the next 90 days is:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Use TwinSight X500 as the proof asset to enter real-time 3D, Unity WebGL, technical visualization, digital twin, simulation, and Unity Technical Artist conversations, while using ARA and Python tooling only as secondary evidence of automation capability.
\end{mdcode}




The first offer does not need to be perfect. It must satisfy:




\begin{enumerate}
\item compensation above the minimum threshold;
\item role fit with the portfolio direction;
\item acceptable contract risk;
\item remote feasibility from Colombia;
\item ability to build toward USD 3k–6k/month over 12–24 months.
\end{enumerate}




If an offer fails these criteria, it is not automatically a strategic win even if it is international.
